Hide geoframes from plots

Source: R/visible.R
hide_geoframes_geoscale.Rd

A geoframe can be needed for calculation without being something to show: grid cells that carry the weights, or clusters used to build a crosswalk. hide_geoframes_geoscale() marks such geoframes, and gg_geoscale(), autoplot() and plot() then leave them out unless asked. Nothing else changes: recasts, joins and navigation use every geoframe as before, and the identity of the object (geoscale_id()) is the same.

Usage

hide_geoframes_geoscale(x, geoframes)

show_geoframes_geoscale(x, geoframes = NULL)

Arguments

x

A GeoScale.

geoframes

Character vector of geoframe names. In show_geoframes_geoscale(), NULL (default) shows all.

Value

The GeoScale, with its hidden set changed. The current sets are read with geoscale_geoframes(x, visible = TRUE) and geoscale_geoframes(x, visible = FALSE).

Details

show_geoframes_geoscale() reverses it, for the named geoframes or for all of them. At least one geoframe always stays visible.

See also

geoscale_geoframes(), gg_geoscale()

Examples

gs <- hide_geoframes_geoscale(geoscale_example(), "cell")
gs
#> GeoScale: example 
#> Description: Synthetic example: reused code, non-nesting geoframe pair, and an unassigned leaf 
#> Geoframes (4, coarsest first):
#>   - country (2)  [1 leaf region(s) unassigned]
#>     - state (3)  [1 leaf region(s) unassigned]
#>       - zone (3)  [1 leaf region(s) unassigned]
#>         - cell (7)
#> Leaves: 7
#> Weights: km2, pop (default: km2)
#> Hidden in plots: cell
geoscale_geoframes(gs, visible = TRUE)
#> [1] "country" "state"   "zone"   
geoscale_geoframes(gs, visible = FALSE)
#> [1] "cell"
# calculations still reach the hidden geoframe
geoscale_regions(gs, "cell")
#> [1] "A1"  "A2"  "A3"  "A4"  "A5"  "A6"  "ROW"
geoscale_geoframes(show_geoframes_geoscale(gs), visible = FALSE)
#> character(0)
